shortcut: CORS preflight failure blocking frontend API calls
detail: When the backend API does not properly handle CORS preflight OPTIONS requests, the browser blocks all cross-origin API calls from the frontend. This appears as opaque network errors in the browser console with no useful error message. The failure is caused by missing or misconfigured Access-Control-Allow headers on the backend, or nginx reverse proxy stripping CORS headers. This cross-domain error involves frontend browser security, backend API configuration, and nginx proxy setup. Prerequisite: understanding CORS protocol and browser security model. Requires coordinated CORS configuration across frontend, backend, and proxy layers. To mitigate: test CORS with actual browser requests in CI, not just node fetch. Fix: configure CORS middleware on the backend with correct allowed origins, ensure nginx passes through CORS headers, test with vitest and a real browser environment.
